THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
The claimant as well as the insurer are in appeal.
2. The claimant was a driver in the KSRTC.
When he was riding his motorcycle on 16.04.2014, he suffered an accident when another motorcycle collided with his motorcycle.
As a result of this accident, the claimant has suffered severe injuries to his right leg including a fracture of the right patella which was implanted artificially.
3. It was his case that his right knee had become dysfunctional and he could not continue his services, continue to discharge his services as a driver in the KSRTC.

The case of the insurer is that the accident between the two motorcycles occurred as a result of negligence on the part of the claimant also and therefore the Tribunal ought to have denied him compensation on account of his contribution.

5. It may be pertinent to state here that after the accident and the injury, the KSRTC had proceeded to terminate the services of the claimant for unauthorized absenteeism by an order dated 06.01.2007.
In this order, it is recorded that the claimant was being dismissed for his unauthorized absence from 16.02.2015 to 25.01.2016 i.e., about 10 months of the accident.
6. The claimant challenged the dismissal order by approaching the Labour Court.

The Labour Court,
after conducting an enquiry, proceeded to set aside the award and directed the reinstatement of the claimant.

However, back wages was denied but continuity of service was granted with a direction to The Manager Oriental vs Ramesh And Anr on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101336048/
3 provide an alternative job to him.

sentences.text:
While setting aside the order of the dismissal, the Tribunal as recorded as follows:
"Considering the principles relied upon in above said citations and the facts of the present case, it is crystal clear that, the absence of petitioner from his duties was not at all intentional one but because of the accident suffered by him.
It is also an admitted fact that, petitioner can not discharge his duty as Driver because of the said accident.
Hence, respondent has to provide alternative lighter job to petitioner for his future work.
However, it is to be noted here that, as petitioner was not worked for these period, he is not entitled for back wages on the principles of "no work no pay".
But petitioner is entitled for reinstatement with continuity of service with a direction that respondent should provide alternative lighter job to petitioner.

Accordingly,
issue No.2 is answered in the negative."

8. It is thus clear that the Labour Court has recorded a positive finding that the claimant could not discharge his NC: 2024:KHC-K:6897 duty as a driver and his unauthorized absence was because of the injuries caused to him in the accident.
9. The Tribunal has also given a finding regarding the conduct of the claimant in the following terms:
"17. It is to be noted here that respondent had given Silver Medal to petitioner for his satisfactory service in the year 2006.
Admittedly, petitioner was working in the respondent Corporation since from 1999 and there was no allegation of absenteeism against him till 2014.
Only after petitioner sustained accident on 16.10.2014, he could not attend his duties.
Hence, his absence from duty for 16.02.2015 to 25.01.2016 was not intentional one.

Subsequently, when petitioner came to know that he cannot drive the vehicles, he had given application to change the cadre of job or at least alternatively he had given application praying for voluntary retirement.

However,
without considering any of these documents, respondent removed the petitioner from service.

This shows that, the act or conduct of respondent in dismissing the petitioner from service is harsh compared to the absence of the petitioner, his NC:
2024:KHC-K:6897 absence is not intentional one, but because of injuries sustained by him in the accident.

This fact would have been considered by the respondent while passing the final order, but respondent did not do so."
10.

The conjoint reading of the above paragraphs would indicate that the claimant was discharging his services as a driver in an exemplary manner, which had secured him a silver medal and the fact that there was no allegation of absenteeism till 2014 i.e., the date of the accident, by itself goes to show that the conduct of the claimant was above board.

sentences.text:
11. As far as the appeal of the insurer that the claimant had contributed to the accident is concerned,
the claim the insurer did not choose to adduce the evidence of the rider of the other motorcycle.
Furthermore, the police after investigation, have formed an opinion that the rider of the other motorcycle was responsible and have laid a charge against them.
In this view of the matter, the contention of the insurer that the claimant had contributed the accident NC: 2024:KHC-K:6897 cannot be accepted and the appeal of the insurer is therefore dismissed.
12. The Tribunal has, however, come to the conclusion that the claimant could not be intended for loss of future income in the light of the fact that he was a driver in the KSRTC.
However, as noticed above, the claimant lost his job because of the injuries that he suffered in the accident and there is a judicial finding that his absence was due to the injury.

It is therefore clear that for this period, that is from 16.02.2015 to 25.01.2016 and then from 06.01.2017 to 29.10.2018 i.e., till the date of the award directing his reinstatement i.e., for a period of 33 months in all he would be entitled for loss of income.
13. The order of dismissal which is produced along with an application for additional documents indicates that the claimant was earning a sum of Rs.27,197/- as on the date of his termination.
Consequently, for this period of 33 months, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.8,97,501/-.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

In my view, having regard to the injuries suffered and the fact that the claimant was not able to resume his duties as a driver, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.75,000 towards loss of amenities.

15. Since the claimant has been reinstated and has also attained the age of superannuation, no sums are awarded towards loss of future income except the amounts awarded above for the loss of income during the period during the aforementioned period for which the claimant suffered an order of termination.
16. The sum of Rs.1,50,000/- awarded towards medical expenses and sum of Rs.45,000/- awarded towards leave encashment is affirmed.
17. The sum of Rs.10,000/- awarded towards attendant diet, conveyance and other charges is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.12,67,501/- as against Rs.2,40,000/-, along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
19. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

20. Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered and the resultant effects on the claimant, it would be appropriate to direct that the entire amount of compensation awarded by this order shall be invested in - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6897 the fixed deposit in the name of the claimant for a period of ten years and the claimant will be entitled to withdraw the interest periodically.
The remaining sum shall be disbursed to him on proper identification.
21. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award forthwith.
The appeal of the claimant is accordingly allowed in part.
